derives_from: Punjabi has no published pronunciation key of the kind Bhargava's dictionary gives Hindi, so this table adapts the mechanism rather than a book: it is generated from `hi__hi-IN.json` -- which follows Bhargava's page layout and the *Rapidex English Speaking Course*'s letter-for-sound choices -- with every Devanagari letter mapped to its Gurmukhi counterpart and five overrides that are facts about Gurmukhi rather than preferences. See content/RESPELL-SYSTEMS.md and tmp/punjabi.md. The layout is the one an Indian reader has met: hyphens dividing syllables, a prime after the stressed one, ordinary Gurmukhi letters, a one-line legend.

deviations.rule: Gurmukhi writes the virama only before a subjoined ਹ ਰ ਵ
deviations.why: **The largest thing this table does differently from Hindi's, and it is Gurmukhi's own orthography rather than a simplification.** Devanagari writes नमस्ते and स्टेशन with a virama and a half-form; Punjabi writes ਨਮਸਤੇ, ਸਟੇਸ਼ਨ, ਪਲੇਟਫ਼ਾਰਮ, ਪਾਸਪੋਰਟ and ਟਿਕਟ with bare letters. So every consonant has one spelling here where Hindi's has three, ੍ survives only in front of ਰ (ਪ੍ਰੀਪੇਡ, ਟ੍ਰੇਨ, ਸ੍ਰੀ), and the whole class of forgotten-virama defect that dominated the Bengali, Tamil and Telugu tables cannot occur. What carries the information instead is the syllable hyphen: ਨ-ਮਸ-ਤੇ says which letter closes which syllable, and an onset cluster gets the epenthetic vowel a Punjabi reader supplies anyway -- which is exactly what Punjabi does with an English loan.

Punjabi orthography has ਖ਼ ਗ਼ ਜ਼ ਫ਼ and no ਕ਼, and no Punjabi speaker distinguishes /q/ from /k/, so /q/ is ਕ. The other four are kept because /x ɣ z f/ really do occur in Punjabi's Perso-Arabic vocabulary. ड़ and ढ़ both become ੜ, Punjabi's own flap.

deviations.rule: श and ष both spell ਸ਼
deviations.why: Gurmukhi has no retroflex sibilant. /ʂ/ and /ʃ/ therefore merge, which is what Punjabi does with a Sanskrit loan (ਭਾਸ਼ਾ, ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼) and the documented cost of this table.

approximations: Sounds with no Gurmukhi letter, and what they get. /ʔ/ and /ʕ/ are written as nothing, which is what Punjabi already does with Arabic hamza and ain (ਅਰਬ, ਇਸਲਾਮ) and which leaves a Thai zero onset correctly bare. /ħ/ is ਹ. /θ ð/ are ਥ ਦ, colliding with /t̪ d/ for the dental targets. /x ɣ/ are ਖ਼ ਗ਼, which is better than Hindi manages -- it converts them to /kʰ ɡ/ and writes ਖ ਗ -- because Punjabi's own orthography carries the two letters. /q/ is ਕ. /y yː ʉ/ are ਯੂ and /ɵ/ is ਯੋ. /ɛ/ and /æ/ are both ਐ, which keeps the vowel's quality at the cost of its length; Hindi gives /ɛ/ ए and loses the quality instead. /ɔ ɔː ɒ/ are ਔ, a real Punjabi letter where Hindi has to borrow the candra-o. Tone is not written: 30 of the 33 tables drop the Chao letters by policy and this is one of them, because a Punjabi reader shown a tone bar on a German word would read neither.
note:
**Gurmukhi is the one Brahmic script in this corpus that does not write the virama, and that is the design of this table.** A consonant letter already says [ə], as in Devanagari, but a coda and a cluster are written as bare letters rather than with a virama or a half-form -- ਨਮਸਤੇ, ਸਟਾਪ, ਟਿਕਟ -- so each consonant has exactly one spelling and the syllable hyphen tells the reader where the vowel is not. ੍ appears only before ਰ, which is the one cluster Punjabi really conjoins.

Three things are Punjabi's own. The **addak** ੱ writes a geminate on the preceding syllable (ਪੱ-ਤਾ, ਅੱ-ਖ), which matters because gemination is phonemic in Punjabi and because `ː` is dropped by most tables. The **tippi/bindi** choice is orthographic and mechanical -- ੰ over a bare consonant and over ਿ ੁ ੂ, ਂ after ਾ ੀ ੇ ੈ ੋ ੌ -- and is made by one fixup rather than in fifty rules. And **ਔ and ਐ are real letters for [ɔ] and [ɛ]**, so this table borrows nothing where Hindi's has to reach for a candra vowel.

There is **no bare `ʰ` rule**, deliberately: Hindi's `ʰ` -> "" is what let ধন্যবাদ print with its aspiration silently gone, because both halves of `dʰ` were mapped. Every aspirate has a rule of its own here, so an aspirate this table does not know prints a raw IPA modifier and `--gaps` catches it.
legend: ’ ਤੋਂ ਪਹਿਲੇ ਹਿੱਸੇ ਉੱਤੇ ਜ਼ੋਰ ਦਿਓ। ਬਾਕੀ ਸਭ ਆਮ ਗੁਰਮੁਖੀ ਹੈ — ਕੋਈ ਨਵਾਂ ਚਿੰਨ੍ਹ ਨਹੀਂ।
